# Error codes

<!-- Code generated by internal/errcode/generrors. DO NOT EDIT. -->
<!-- Edit the registry in src/cli/internal/errcode/registry_*.go and run `go generate ./...`. -->

Every user-facing hatchward error carries a code. Quote it verbatim in a
bug report — the wording of a message may change between releases, the code
will not.

The code appears in the error hatchward prints.

## ECMD — Commands

| Code | Meaning | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ECMD001` | That command needs a sub-command. | See the help text just printed, and run one of the sub-commands it lists. |
| `ECMD002` | A required argument or option was not supplied. | Pass the argument or flag named in the message. |
| `ECMD003` | An argument or option was given a value it does not accept. | Use one of the values listed in the message. |
| `ECMD004` | The operation was cancelled at the confirmation prompt. | Re-run and answer `y`, or pass the flag named in the message to skip the prompt. |
| `ECMD005` | hatchward hit an internal error. | Report it with this code and the command that produced it. |
| `ECMD006` | A question was never answered — the input ended first. | Re-run on a terminal, or feed the command a script with an answer for every question it asks. |

## EGRS — Egress proxy

| Code | Meaning | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `EGRS001` | The egress proxy allowlist or startup options are invalid. | Check runtime.egressAllow for anything other than exact lowercase hostnames, and that the proxy was started with a CA and allowlist configured. |
| `EGRS002` | The egress proxy could not mint its certificate authority or a per-connection leaf certificate. | Retry the assignment; if the error persists, update Hatchward and report this code. |
| `EGRS003` | The egress proxy could not bind its listener or reach an upstream host. | Check that the runner can bind a loopback port and resolve and reach the allowlisted hosts; a name that resolves only to a private or link-local address is refused on purpose. |

## EIOX — Filesystem

| Code | Meaning | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `EIOX001` | A directory could not be created. | Check that the parent directory exists and is writable by the user running hatchward. |
| `EIOX002` | A lock file could not be opened. | Check that the directory is writable by the user running hatchward. |
| `EIOX003` | A lock could not be acquired. | If this persists, report it with this code. |
| `EIOX004` | Another hatchward process is using this data. | Wait for the other process to finish, then try again. |
| `EIOX005` | A file could not be read. | Check that the file is readable by the user running hatchward. |
| `EIOX006` | A file's contents could not be read as valid data. | If this persists, report it with this code. |
| `EIOX007` | Data could not be prepared for writing. | Report it with this code. |
| `EIOX008` | A temporary file could not be created. | Check free space and that the directory is writable by the user running hatchward. |
| `EIOX009` | A file could not be written. | Check free space and that the directory is writable by the user running hatchward. |
| `EIOX010` | A file could not be saved. | Check that the directory is writable by the user running hatchward. |

## ERUN — Hosted runner

| Code | Meaning | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ERUN001` | The runner identity could not be created or loaded safely. | Check that the Hatchward home is writable, private to your user, and that runner.identity is a regular 0600 file. |
| `ERUN002` | The local runner configuration is unavailable or invalid. | Check runner.yml against the documented local override fields and keep it readable only by your user. |
| `ERUN003` | A runner protocol value is malformed. | Retry enrollment with a newly issued code; if the error persists, update Hatchward and report this code. |
| `ERUN004` | The hosted runner API request or response failed validation. | Check the configured HTTPS API endpoint and connectivity, then retry; if the service returned an invalid response, report this code. |

## ESVC — Boot services

| Code | Meaning | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ESVC001` | There is no user session manager to install a boot service into. | Start `hatchward` by hand after each boot, or run it under whatever already supervises services on this host. |
| `ESVC002` | A path the boot service would name cannot safely be installed. | Move the hatchward binary into a directory only your own user can write, or run `chmod g-w,o-w` on that directory, then install again. |
| `ESVC003` | The boot service's unit file could not be written or removed. | Check that your home directory is writable, then run `hatchward service install` again. |
| `ESVC004` | The supervisor refused to load or unload the boot service. | Run the reported command yourself to see what the supervisor says, then run `hatchward service install` again. |
| `ESVC005` | The service was installed, but it will start at login rather than at boot. | Run `loginctl enable-linger` for this account with the privileges it asks for, or pass --linger=false to accept a service that starts at login. |
